clue.text: Mayfair exposé bodes evil, stir it up

indicators.note: to stir something up is to churn it around, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the fodder as printed lacks one I that the title needs

explanation.surface: A society scandal-sheet about Mayfair warns of trouble and urges someone to make a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir it up' rearranges BODES EVIL, but those nine letters are one I short of the title, so the setter has slipped. Evelyn Waugh's novel satirises the Bright Young Things of Mayfair, London's smartest district.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh's 1930 satire lays bare the frivolous party set of fashionable London society.

clue.text: Orbiting quirk from Wakefield

parts.note: Tom Wakefield wrote a series of novels about a character surnamed Quirk; the clue asks for her first name, with 'Orbiting' pointing to her circling adventures

explanation.walkthrough: 'quirk' looks like an oddity but is a surname: Tom Wakefield's novels (Trixie Trash, Star Ascending; The Love Siege) follow Isobel Quirk.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Tom Wakefield's novel series bears this forename before her surname Quirk.

clue.text: The panel possibly will identify Kalia Nag

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters given could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A committee is expected to recognise somebody with an exotic name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges THE PANEL. Kala Nag ('Black Snake') is the old elephant in Kipling's story 'Toomai of the Elephants'; the clue spells the name Kalia.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's Kala Nag is a great working beast of the Indian forests with a trunk and tusks.

clue.text: Possibly rid Antonio of admission to the ministry

indicators.note: possibly says the following letters could form something else when reordered

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone should strip Antonio of his right to enter government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges RID and ANTONIO together; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being formally made a priest or minister is how one is admitted to the clergy.

clue.text: Dramatist in Hermione's company

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A playwright is keeping company with Hermione, perhaps from The Winter's Tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Hermione suggests Shakespeare, but the playwright sits inside 'Hermione's company': Eugène Ionesco of the Theatre of the Absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Ionesco was the Romanian-French author of absurdist plays such as Rhinoceros.

clue.text: Farmer's woman

parts.note: refers to the title character of a novel by the Australian writer Beverley Farmer, a woman linked with a marine mammal of selkie legend

explanation.walkthrough: 'Farmer' is not someone who tills the land but Beverley Farmer, whose 1992 novel is The Seal Woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverley Farmer's novel is titled after a selkie figure, a woman named for a sea creature.

clue.text: Ziegler involved with new composer

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone named Ziegler is mixed up with a fresh musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' mixes ZIEGLER with N (new). Giovanni Legrenzi was a seventeenth-century Venetian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Legrenzi was a Baroque Italian who wrote operas and church music at St Mark's, Venice.

clue.text: "Reverse cannot befall / That fine —— / Whose Sources are interior" (Emily Dickinson)

definitions.text: "Reverse cannot befall / That fine —— / Whose Sources are interior" (Emily Dickinson)

parts.words: "Reverse cannot befall / That fine —— / Whose Sources are interior" (Emily Dickinson)
parts.note: a quotation from an Emily Dickinson poem with one word missing, the gap to be filled by the solver

explanation.walkthrough: A literary fill-in: the missing word in Dickinson's lines is a noun for thriving or good fortune, the opposite of 'Reverse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickinson contrasts misfortune with inner flourishing and well-being whose springs lie within.

clue.text: "Sought by all means, therefore, how to and hold thee to me firmest" (Milton, Samson Agonistes)

definitions.text: "Sought by all means, therefore, how to and hold thee to me firmest" (Milton, Samson Agonistes)

parts.words: "Sought by all means, therefore, how to and hold thee to me firmest" (Milton, Samson Agonistes)
parts.note: a line from Milton's Samson Agonistes with a word left out, for the solver to supply

explanation.walkthrough: A literary fill-in: Dalila tells Samson she sought how to make him love her and keep him close; the missing verb means win affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalila's speech needs a verb for making oneself loved and cherished by another.

clue.text: Missile in Gallico's adventure

definitions.meaning: a US submarine-launched ballistic weapon named after the Greek sea god
Paul Gallico's novel The ___ Adventure, about a capsized ocean liner

explanation.surface: A rocket features in a thrilling story by Paul Gallico.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses share the Greek sea god's name: a Cold War submarine missile and Gallico's 1969 disaster novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of the sea lent his name to a ballistic missile and to Gallico's overturned liner.

clue.text: Often found stuck in some book or other

definitions.text: Often found stuck in some book or other

parts.words: Often found stuck in some book or other
parts.note: describes a label pasted inside a book's front cover to show who owns it

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase 'from the books of' is printed on a bookplate, the owner's label glued inside the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookplate bearing the Latin 'from the library of' is pasted inside the covers of many volumes.

clue.text: Jumble sale for iconic lioness

indicators.note: jumble means a muddle, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A rummage sale raising money for a famous big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumble sale' reads as a charity event, but 'Jumble' rearranges SALE. Elsa is the lioness raised by Joy Adamson in Born Free.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy Adamson's book Born Free made the orphaned lioness she raised world-famous.

clue.text: Ben's posthumous curse against fire god

definitions.text: Ben's posthumous curse against fire god

parts.words: Ben's posthumous curse against fire god
parts.note: points to Ben Jonson's poem railing at Vulcan after a fire destroyed his papers, published after his death

explanation.walkthrough: Ben is Ben Jonson, whose 'An Execration upon Vulcan' curses the Roman god of fire for burning his library; it appeared in print after his death.
explanation.definitionFit: The word in Jonson's title means a solemn denunciation or curse, here aimed at Vulcan.

clue.text: Granting admission to Powell's world

definitions.meaning: agreeing to receive someone or something
Anthony Powell's novel The ___ World, from A Dance to the Music of Time

explanation.surface: Letting someone in to the society Anthony Powell describes.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Powell's The Acceptance World (1955) is the third volume of A Dance to the Music of Time.
explanation.definitionFit: Receiving or admitting someone, and the title word of Powell's third Dance volume.

clue.text: She made a hell of a marriage, and became queen of the underworld

definitions.text: She made a hell of a marriage, and became queen of the underworld

parts.words: She made a hell of a marriage, and became queen of the underworld
parts.note: the Roman goddess carried off by the god of the dead to be his wife in Hades

explanation.walkthrough: 'a hell of a marriage' is literal: the Roman Persephone was abducted by Pluto and wed in the underworld, where she reigned as queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman name for Persephone, seized by Pluto to rule beside him over the dead.

clue.text: His work recalls Oscar in Paris

definitions.text: His work recalls Oscar in Paris

parts.words: His work recalls Oscar in Paris
parts.note: a sculptor who carved the tomb of Oscar Wilde in Père Lachaise cemetery, Paris

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests a film award, but it is Oscar Wilde, whose winged tomb in Paris is by Sir Jacob Epstein.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein carved Wilde's monumental grave at Père Lachaise in 1912.

clue.text: Underwater high temperature described by laureate?

parts.note: what lies under the water's surface is the ocean, taken here as the open sea
a fever is a raised body temperature

explanation.surface: A diver's overheating, as recounted by a poet laureate.
explanation.walkthrough: The laureate is John Masefield, whose poem 'Sea-Fever' begins 'I must go down to the seas again'.
explanation.definitionFit: Masefield, Poet Laureate from 1930, wrote of a longing for the ocean in his best-known poem.

clue.text: He made overtures to expatriate girl and Swiss patriot

definitions.text: He made overtures to expatriate girl and Swiss patriot

parts.words: He made overtures to expatriate girl and Swiss patriot
parts.note: an Italian composer whose operas include one about an Italian girl in Algiers and one about William Tell

explanation.walkthrough: 'made overtures' looks like courting but means writing opera overtures: L'italiana in Algeri (the expatriate girl) and William Tell (the Swiss patriot).
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini composed L'italiana in Algeri and Guillaume Tell, both famed for their overtures.

clue.text: Point of departure for one thus obliged to leave by Norris?

definitions.text: Point of departure for one thus obliged to leave by Norris?

parts.words: Point of departure for one thus obliged to leave by Norris?
parts.note: a Chinese port whose name became a verb for drugging or tricking a man aboard ship, as happens in a Frank Norris novel

explanation.walkthrough: The city is also the verb for kidnapping a sailor; in Frank Norris's Moran of the Lady Letty the hero is carried off to sea that way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese port gave its name to press-ganging, so it is both a departure point and the method.

clue.text: Forsake Crouch's work

definitions.meaning: to desert or give up entirely
A 2009 thriller by the American novelist Blake Crouch

explanation.surface: Give up on a writer's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake Crouch is an American thriller writer; one of his novels has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave behind or desert, and the title of a Blake Crouch novel.

clue.text: Inexpensive, like Locke's Christianity?

definitions.meaning: John Locke wrote The Reasonableness of Christianity (1695)

explanation.surface: Cheap, as a philosopher found his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: John Locke's treatise The Reasonableness of Christianity argued faith was consistent with reason; the question mark flags the adjective formed from its title.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair price is one that is moderate, and Locke argued that faith was rational.

clue.text: He lends support in final lyric of Keats

indicators.note: in shows that the answer is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A friend is helpfully mentioned in the poet's last song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final lyric' looks like a hunt through Keats's poems, but the answer sits across 'finAL LYric'.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or confederate is someone who stands by you and helps.

clue.text: California city thug in Stacpoole's pool

parts.note: LA is short for Los Angeles
a goon is a hired heavy

explanation.surface: A heavy from Los Angeles turns up in a novel set by a pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here, not a container. H. de Vere Stacpoole wrote The Blue Lagoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacpoole's novel The Blue Lagoon is named for a sheltered stretch of water inside a reef.

clue.text: As an actor, the betting is on a Scot

parts.note: SP is the starting price in horse-race betting
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Bookmakers are backing a Scotsman in a theatrical role.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the odds on a horse when a race begins; Ian is the Scottish form of John.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to drama and acting, from Thespis, the reputed first Greek stage performer.

clue.text: Locals where many like Mortimer have been called to the bar

definitions.meaning: in Britain a local is one's neighbourhood pub

definitions.text: where many like Mortimer have been called to the bar
definitions.meaning: barristers such as John Mortimer are called to the bar by the ... of Court

explanation.surface: Pubs where lawyers have been summoned to the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: A British 'local' is your nearest pub. John Mortimer (creator of Rumpole) was a barrister, and barristers qualify through London's Inns of Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverns are pubs, and the Inns of Court are the four legal societies admitting barristers.

clue.text: Novelist shows crew submerged in quiet river

indicators.note: something submerged in a river lies within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Don, from Sholokhov's novel And Quiet Flows the Don
a rowing eight is a boat crew

explanation.surface: A writer reveals a rowing team sinking in a calm stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Len Deighton is the spy novelist; 'quiet river' nods to Sholokhov's And Quiet Flows the Don.
explanation.definitionFit: Len Deighton wrote spy fiction such as The IPCRESS File.

clue.text: Dream king from Weber

definitions.meaning: the fairy king in A Midsummer Night's Dream
Carl Maria von Weber's last opera is named after this fairy king

explanation.surface: A monarch seen in a vision comes from the composer Weber.
explanation.walkthrough: Dream is Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream; Weber's 1826 opera shares the fairy king's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's fairy monarch, husband of Titania, also gives Weber's final opera its title.

clue.text: Sonnets, as I modified, expressed feelings

indicators.note: modified says the letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Poems I altered conveyed my emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges SONNETS, AS and I; 'expressed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Perceptions or physical impressions are what the senses register as emotions or sensory responses.
